classification_extension_record.iid_rationale: Unlike the district-level rice yield panel data (which has explicit spatio-temporal autocorrelations and annual macro-climatic shifts requiring strict chronological partitioning), the multi-class crop recommendation task operates on localized, point-in-time soil physicochemical characteristics (N, P, K, pH) and micro-climatic readings (temperature, humidity, rainfall). Each row represents an agronomic laboratory sample / environmental profile mapped to an optimal crop label without longitudinal district time-series tracking. Consequently, random stratified splitting (60% train, 20% validation, 20% test) across the 22 balanced crop classes (100 observations per class) preserves class balance across partitions without violating temporal causality. This independence justification is logged explicitly before unblocking stratified splitting.
